channel.title: Teppei Nakano — Blog
channel.description: Notes on medical ML, local LLMs, and air-gapped AI

item.title: Split medical ML by patient, not by row
item.description: The same person’s stays in train and test memorize the person, not the disease. Group by patient id; cut by time when you can.

item.title: Do not mix future notes into an EHR prediction
item.description: A discharge summary and post-outcome labs are not prediction. Freeze time t; keep only what was observed by then.

item.title: Do not lead a rare-event paper with AUROC alone
item.description: At low prevalence, high discrimination still pages mostly misses. Put precision and alert counts on the same table.

item.title: The dangerous guideline RAG error is a cited hallucination
item.description: Keep exceptions in the same chunk. Do not emit withdrawn doses. Score faithfulness to the document, not “correctness.”

item.title: A hospital LLM is about not sending, first
item.description: Regex de-id still re-identifies. Do not SFT on raw notes. Identifiers live on RAG metadata.

item.title: Talk-to-note is not a BLEU task
item.description: Fluency hides added and dropped facts. The teacher is the progress note right after the talk. Do not fluently “fix” ASR.

item.title: Do not mean-impute the chart
item.description: Why it was not measured can be the severity. Keep a mask and time since last observation.

item.title: ICD-supervised “diagnosis” often reproduces billing
item.description: Suspected, history, and primary are allowed to differ. Name weak labels; do not hire if human spans drop.

item.title: Radiology-report NLP is negation and time
item.description: Half the findings are absences. If text enters an imaging task, acquisition time and report time must agree.

item.title: Medical-image scores die on the next scanner
item.description: Suspect reconstruction and protocol before disease shift. An embedding that predicts site will be used by the disease model.

item.title: Is your RNA-seq model predicting the kit?
item.description: Batch can outrun biology. Put correction order and a cross-study split before the learner.

item.title: How much heterogeneity can one biopsy support?
item.description: The observation is partial. Diversity inside the sample and unseen regions need different teachers. Do not split across a patient’s other sites.

item.title: MoE compute is sparse; memory is not
item.description: A router picks experts per token. Capacity is large; collapse kills the sparsity. Do not borrow a dense sizing equation.

item.title: FlashAttention is I/O, not an approximation
item.description: Do not materialize the O(T²) score matrix. Same softmax, finished in SRAM. The win is long prefill, not one-token decode.

item.title: KV cache fills VRAM before the weights do
item.description: Under concurrency and long context, weights are not what runs out. What MHA / MQA / GQA actually reduce, from the memory equation.

item.title: What quantization kills first
item.description: GPTQ, AWQ, and FP8 all throw information away. They differ in which information, and in how calibration drift shows up on names and long context.

item.title: Why DPO comes after SFT
item.description: SFT moves a distribution; DPO orders two outputs. Skip a step and you keep honorifics and lose refusal.

item.title: Cut RAG “accuracy” into four layers
item.description: Do not fold retrieval, use, answer, and refusal into one score. Split recall@k from faithfulness, and keep a refusal set as large as the answer set.

item.title: Half of RAG misses are chunk boundaries
item.description: Too big averages; too small cuts the referent. Metadata is a filter; the vector is the body.

item.title: RoPE in LLMs, from the rotation up
item.description: Do not add a position vector — rotate Q and K. Why the relative offset survives the inner product, and what breaks when you stretch context.

item.title: Windows and attention sinks throw the past away
item.description: Not the same as stretching RoPE. Policy outside the window is politely violated. Sink or re-inject.

item.title: Speculative decoding is an acceptance-rate game
item.description: A draft model writes ahead; the large model verifies without changing its distribution. Low acceptance and you are only hosting two models.

item.title: Temperature is not a sampling policy
item.description: Temperature is softmax sharpness; top-k and top-p decide the cut. Do not eval at 0.8 and serve at 0.2. Quote T, k, and p together.

item.title: Pick LoRA layers before you pick rank
item.description: Rank is the dimension of the update subspace. Start with q,v, then the MLP. “It’s LoRA, so it won’t forget” is false.

item.title: RMSNorm and pre-norm are why deep LLMs stand up
item.description: From why BatchNorm fails on sequences, to RMSNorm without a mean, pre-norm residuals, and SwiGLU.

item.title: Why decoder-only won the local box
item.description: Match train and serve, keep one objective, keep one box. Bidirectional still wins some understand-only jobs.

item.title: Distillation copies a distribution, not an answer key
item.description: Pass teacher logits via KL. Keep hard refusals. For draft models, measure acceptance, not loss.

item.title: BPE cuts quietly break SKUs and Japanese
item.description: The vocabulary is not words. Read digit, full-width, and proper-name splits before you talk parameters.

item.title: InfoNCE is the common language of embeddings
item.description: Dense retrieval and CLIP are a classify-the-positive loss. Negatives set the representation. Do not use a generator’s hidden states as a retriever unchanged.

item.title: 0.9 is not nine times in ten
item.description: Confidence is not calibration. ECE and temperature scaling. Do not treat cosine or post-DPO logits as probabilities.

item.title: A public bench score is not a synonym for smart
item.description: Contamination and shift are different. Hire from an in-house set plus overlap with the train corpus.

item.title: Why Transformers still train with AdamW
item.description: Adaptive second moment, and weight decay decoupled from the gradient. Leave Norm γ out of decay.

item.title: What to decide first for an air-gapped local LLM
item.description: A checklist of decisions to lock down before picking a model, when the stack cannot call any external API.

item.title: Opening this blog
item.description: I added a Markdown-powered blog to this portfolio. Notes on air-gapped LLMs and machine learning will live here.

item.title: How to add a post
item.description: Drop one Markdown file and add one entry to posts.json. No build step.
